title: Precision-profile load harness for long-tail quantization tradeoffs (FP16/INT8/INT4)
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a reproducible, production-oriented harness that systematically benchmarks model precision configurations (FP16, INT8, INT4) across realistic and long-tail conversational/summarization workloads. The harness must measure tokens/sec throughput, latency p50/p95/p99, memory and GPU utilization, KV cache hit behavior, and application-level quality signals (embedding cosine, ROUGE/chrF for summarization, and a small golden prompt accuracy set). We will run a combinatorial matrix of quantization knobs + batch sizes + sequence-length distributions and produce per-variant regression detection alerts and artifact bundles for offline analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can replay production trace slices and a curated long-tail prompt corpus to generate deterministic runs
Metrics exported to S3/Grafana: tokens_sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU_mem_peak, kv_cache_hit_rate, embedding_cosine, rouge_l_delta
Regression rules implemented: (tokens_sec drop >= 8% AND p95 increase >= 15%) OR (embedding_cosine drop >= 0.02 OR rouge_l drop >= 3) will mark a run as failed
CI gating in place: a failing regression blocks the model-quant PR and posts a detailed artifact link
Dashboard panels and a CSV report generator exist for matrix comparisons and dimensioned graphs (by model, quant, batch, seq_len)
Reproducible seed & config snapshot attached to every run artifact
implementation_steps: Design long-tail corpus: sample production traces, add synthesized corner-case prompts, categorize by intent/length
Create runner that launches quantization variants in parallel using existing runtime perf harness (reuse ENG-40127 runner hooks where possible)
Instrument metrics: tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99, GPU/CPU, KV cache metrics, and quality evalers (embedding cosine + ROUGE)
Define regression thresholds with PM/SRE and add automated alerting + rollback annotations
Integrate artifacts to CI: store model tarball, quant-config, metrics CSVs, and a human-readable summary to S3; post link to PR
Add Grafana dashboards and a lightweight UI to filter matrix by workload class and highlight failed cells
notes: 2026-02-17: Kickoff - scoped long-tail prompt classes (dialogue, multi-turn follow-up, summarization, codegen edge cases)
2026-02-22: Skeleton runner merged - ENG branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/pull/214 (initial matrix orchestration)
2026-02-25: Draft regression rules discussed with PM (A. Nguyen) and SRE (L. Gomez) - agreed conservative defaults; need validation vs baseline runs

2026-02-28: First end-to-end run completed across FP16/INT8 for smaller model; observed systematic p95 tail increases on INT4 for long sequences - captured artifact: s3://redwood-bench/artifacts/ENG-99531/run-2026-02-28.zip
Open items: finalize acceptance thresholds (PM feedback), add adaptive sampling for extreme tail prompts, add KV-cache warmup policy to runner to reduce noisy variance
risks_and_tradeoffs: INT4 yields large throughput gains but occasionally fails quality thresholds on multi-turn summarization prompts -> tradeoff requires per-workload gating
Aggressive batching improves tokens/sec but amplifies p95 for short-latency SLOs; will need workload-aware batching recommendations
Synthetic long-tail augmentation may not perfectly mirror production failure modes; we will keep traffic-replay as the primary signal
review_feedback: PM (A. Nguyen): prefer conservative quality thresholds for now, must include per-customer opt-out for lower-precision rollouts
Design (J. Park): dashboard should surface a heatmap view with clickable cells that open run artifacts
SRE (L. Gomez): require run-level reproducibility metadata (git sha, seed, quant-config) and a TTL for stored artifacts
next_steps: Lock down acceptance thresholds with PM and run full matrix across standard models (due 2026-03-10)
Add adaptive sampling and tail-only replication to reduce compute cost for repeated runs
Prepare CI gating integration PR and add a canary stage that runs on a nightly cadence
